notes:
# A link copied out of an email keeps its passcode {link}
A Zoom link carries the passcode in it, and three things that happen to a
link between an invitation and the meeting form were quietly throwing it
away — leaving the meeting number intact, so the join went through and Zoom
asked for a passcode, while the same link clicked in the mail app worked
perfectly.

An HTML mail body hands out `&` where the link had `&`, so whatever came
after it was not read as part of the address. Some webmail hands the whole
link over encoded, with no `?` left in it at all. And a link copied out of a
sentence brings the punctuation around it, so a `>` or a `)` ended up on the
end of the passcode itself. All three are now undone as the link goes into
the box, so what you read back is what will be joined.

# The New meeting screen, rearranged {sliders}
What the meeting IS and WHEN it runs now sit side by side rather than one
above the other: they are two different questions, and a schedule card the
full width of the pane was mostly white space. The name and the folder share
a line for the same reason. The two cards are equal halves — same width,
same height — filling whatever the pane gives them up to a point, and going
back to one above the other on a narrow window — about 1300 points wide with
the meeting list at its narrowest, so both shapes are a drag away. They can
also be squeezed:
a card that insists on its width is a floor under the WINDOW, which is why
widening it once left it stuck wide.

Each card leads with a tinted mark and says what it is for on the line under
its name, the Date, Time, Time zone and Folder boxes carry a chevron so they
read as things that open, and a draft says "Draft" beside its title with
"Save meeting" on the button rather than "Save changes" — there are no
changes yet. The Recording card has lost the row that said recording stops
when the meeting ends: it was a row with nothing to press on it, and it is
the card's own sentence now.

# The bottom line says what the recorder is actually doing {clock}
A run waiting in a Zoom waiting room reported "Waiting". The recorder had
written "Waiting to be let in" — that one word is for a list row, which is
narrow, and the line along the bottom of the window is not.

# Glyphs sit on the line of words beside them {sliders}
A mark and a sentence were being lined up by their BOXES -- tops, or
centres -- and a text field's box carries the descender under the letters
and the line's leading above them, so the glyph sat a point or two above
the words it belongs to. Every one of them is now placed on the letters
themselves: the asides under settings, the bordered notes, the schedule's
sentence, the invitation rows, the Date, Time and Time zone fields.

The bar along the bottom of the meeting form and of Settings casts a soft
edge over the page now, rather than being divided from it by a hairline --
the page scrolls underneath it, and that is what that looks like. Its
buttons also sit in the middle of their strip: the band had six points over
them and twenty-two under.

# The empty screen is the right colour in the light {sun}
A folder with nothing in it showed its card in charcoal on a light page, with
black text on it. The card's colour was handed to its layer once, and a
layer keeps whatever colour it was given — so a window drawn while the Mac
was dark stayed dark after the Mac changed its mind. The empty card, the
trial card and the time-zone notice now ask for their colour again, as every
other card in the app already did.

# A new meeting lands in the folder you are looking at {folder}
Press New — or ⌘N — with a folder open and the meeting is filed there
already. It used to arrive unfiled, which put the new row at the top of a
list it was not in: it disappeared the moment it was saved, and had to be
filed by hand afterwards. Unfiled and the ordinary lists leave it unfiled,
which is what they are.

# The folder list reads as a list of places {folder}
The Folders section in the sidebar has been restyled. Its heading is the size
of the rows under it rather than a caption over them, and the + is in a
tinted disc so the one thing on that line that DOES something looks like it.
Every folder keeps its count badge, and the ••• appears on the folder you
are looking at instead of running down the whole column beside those counts.

"No folder" is now "Unfiled", under a hairline, with a line saying what is in
it — it is a place to go and look, not the absence of one, and on most Macs
it holds nearly everything.

# Time zones are named after places, not continents {globe}
The zone picker used to show what the tz database calls a zone —
`America/Los_Angeles`, `America/Tijuana`, `America/Vancouver` — and everybody
reads that first word as the country. Tijuana is Mexico and Vancouver is
Canada. Every row now leads with the city AND the country, says what the zone
is called in words (Pacific Time, Philippine Time), gives the offset for the
meeting's own date, and keeps the IANA name underneath as the thing that is
actually stored. Nothing about the stored value has changed.

Search understands what invitations are written in. A city, a country, a
country's two letters, the IANA name, the friendly name, the abbreviation in
either half of the year — `pst` and `pdt` both find Los Angeles, Vancouver
and Tijuana whatever the season — or an offset typed as `utc-7`, `-0700` or
`utc-07:00`. Where an abbreviation means two things it says so: `pst` puts
the three Pacific cities under "Pacific Time" and Manila under "Other
matches", because Philippine Standard Time is abbreviated PST as well.

And the clock follows the meeting. A meeting set in January says UTC−08:00
for Los Angeles and one in July says UTC−07:00, rather than both being
described as whatever today happens to be.

# The meeting list can be resized again {sliders}
The divider between the list and the meeting beside it could not be moved —
not by dragging, and not by anything else. A split view controller settles
its divider from its panes' own constraints, and this one had settled on a
width it would not leave. The divider now has a grip of the app's own: the
pointer turns into the resize arrows over it, and the list follows the mouse
between 340 points and 460, and a Mac that has never been dragged opens at
the narrowest of those — the meeting beside it is the bigger half. The width
is kept when you let go, so a window left wide opens wide tomorrow. Hiding
and showing the list is unchanged.

# The Automation tabs slide both ways {sliders}
Moving from Finishing back to Joining, the blue pill vanished and reappeared
at the far end instead of travelling. Sliding right it rode over the tabs it
crossed; sliding left it went underneath them, because it happened to be
drawn before they were. It now rides above them whichever way it goes.

# The offer over a meeting says what it will do {video}
Join a Zoom meeting yourself and the panel that appears has been redrawn:
four lines and two buttons. It leads with what it found and that the meeting
is running, asks its question in one line, and then answers the two questions
anybody has before pressing record — what a recording spends while the trial
is running, and what ends up in the file, which was never said at all. That
second one is the Capture setting's own answer, so a Mac set to Entire screen
is told its whole display will be recorded rather than promised otherwise.

"Don't ask again" is a tick beside the buttons rather than a link next to Not
now, where one mis-click turned the feature off for good. It is about the NEXT
meeting: nothing happens until you answer this one, and either answer honours
it. Under it is the way back — the words go to Settings › Automation ▸
Joining, the only time that panel ever brings RecordLah in front of a call.

The panel also arrives WITH the banner inside RecordLah rather than a dozen
seconds after it. It used to wait six seconds of your being in the meeting,
and that wait was only weighed when Zoom was next asked about itself — six
seconds later again. The meeting is confirmed from the meeting window rather
than from Zoom merely being open, so there is nothing left for the wait to
protect against.

# The live banner shimmers in the light too {sparkle}
The band of light that crosses "You're in a meeting" was white at a tenth —
which reads as light sweeping the dark blue banner and as nothing whatever on
the pale one, since that blue is already within a few per cent of white. In
the light appearance the band is now the accent itself: a deeper blue
crossing a pale one. It follows the Mac switching between light and dark
while the app is open.

# Invitations are sorted into what wants you and what does not {envelope}
The Invitations tab was one long list, and the row that actually needed a
person — the invitation whose mail never said when the meeting is — sat in
the middle of it looking like every other row. It is now three piles: Needs
attention, Ready to add, and Already added, with the counts down the side
and a tick for each of the two places the rows come from.

A row that wants something now SAYS what: no date, no start time, or no time
zone. **Set date & time** opens a panel with the same three fields the New
meeting form has — the month grid, the time you can type ("9am", "0900",
"2.15pm") and the zone search — and the meeting arrives armed: it will record
itself, which is what the whole errand is for. A row already in your meetings list stops offering to
be added twice and offers to open the meeting instead.

The connection readings — Full Disk Access, Apple Mail, Calendar — are one
strip along the top instead of a panel, the search row has gained an order to
sort in and is drawn in the app's own controls rather than three stock pop-ups
half the height of the box beside them, and the button now says **Check for
meetings**, because what it does is go and read the mail rather than redraw
the page.

One rule decides both which pile a row is in and whether it arrives armed, so
"Ready to add" means exactly "will arm itself". A meeting whose invitation
gave a date but no start time used to arrive armed against a default hour
nobody chose; it now asks for the time.

# The footer keeps up {clock}
The line along the bottom goes back to naming the next recording a few seconds
after a result. It used to keep "Deleted X" or "Link copied" for the rest of
the session, sitting exactly where the next recording should be.

# A welcome on the first launch {sparkle}
A new Mac now gets one screen explaining the free trial before anything else:
how many recordings it holds, what spends one, and what plainly does not. It
appears after the setup checks have run, so it never lands on top of macOS
asking for Screen Recording.

# A recording has to be a meeting to count {camcorder}
A free recording is spent when a run finishes with at least a minute of
meeting in it. A join that never lands, or a capture that stops after twenty
seconds, costs nothing.

# The automation test stays a test {shield_lock}
Zoom mints the test meeting's link for that one run, so the meeting it leaves
behind is now read-only. Saving it used to drop its two-minute cap, which is
the only thing that ends a run in Zoom's test room.

# A link from a filtered mailbox fits the box {link}
Company mail scanners rewrite every link in an invitation, so what gets
copied out of one is a few hundred characters of scanner wrapper around the
Zoom link. Pasting it now puts the meeting link itself in the box, short
enough to read back and check. The invitation scan has always done this; only
a link pasted by hand kept its wrapper.

# Telegram sets itself up, and proves it {check_circle}
Connecting Telegram used to be two boxes and a paragraph explaining that the
two values come from two different bots. It is now a panel that does the
checking for you: buttons that open BotFather and UserInfoBot, a Paste for the
token, and Telegram asked on the spot whose bot it is — so a token and a chat
ID pasted the wrong way round is caught while you are looking at them. It ends
with Connect & send test, and keeps nothing until that message has actually
arrived on your phone. It also names the step every guide leaves out: open
your own bot and press Start, because Telegram will not let a bot message you
first.

# The title bar reads as one row {sliders}
The tabs sit in a taller capsule with a hairline round it, the way macOS
draws its own, with a divider between the two that are not chosen — and the
blue fill now slides from one tab to the next instead of jumping. The trial
chip is stacked into two lines instead of running a sentence across the bar,
and it lines up with the tabs.

# RecordLah offers to record the meeting you are already in {video}
Join a Zoom meeting or webinar yourself — nothing scheduled, nothing started
here — and a few seconds in, a small panel appears over Zoom asking whether to
record it. Press Record and it starts; there is no link or schedule to set up.
It never takes the keyboard from Zoom, it asks once per meeting, it takes
itself away after a while, and it says what a recording costs while the free
trial is running. "Don't ask again" turns it off for good, and so does Offer to
record under Settings › Automation › Joining.

RecordLah has to be running to notice — it is the app that watches for the
meeting, not the background helper.

# The window can be made small again {sliders}
Once a recording existed, the window refused to be resized below about 2250
points wide — most of a laptop screen and then some. The still on the
recording card was the reason: an image view defends the size of its own
picture, a 960-pixel still therefore put a 960-point floor under a card that
takes just over half the width, and the whole window inherited it. The still
now stretches to whatever room the card has, as it was meant to, and keeps
only its own minimum.

# Closing the window closes the app {check_circle}
The red button shut the window and left RecordLah running with no way back to
it -- not in the Dock, not by opening it again. It now quits, unless a
recording or a join is under way: that carries on in its own process, as it
always has, and clicking the Dock icon brings the window back so you can stop
it or watch it finish.

# Automatic updates keeps its answer {refresh}
The switch under Settings › General showed OFF while updates were in fact
on, and turning it off saved nothing -- it was drawn over a setting nothing
connected it to. It now reads the stored value, marks the page unsaved when
you touch it, and is honoured on the next launch.

# The sidebar's own tidying {folder}
The highlight on the chosen scope or folder was pinned a few points past the
edge of the row, so its right-hand corners were clipped square and the tint
appeared to stop just after the count. It now sits inside the column with its
corners intact and the count within it. The scopes and the Folders section no
longer sit in a white panel of their own on the grey sidebar.

# The free trial chip can be seen in the dark {sparkle}
It was a tenth of the accent colour laid over the title bar, which in dark
mode is a dark grey — so the chip had no edge to it at all. It now uses the
palette's own soft blue, which is a real colour in each appearance, and it
follows the Mac switching between light and dark while the app is open
instead of keeping whichever colour it was built with. The same goes for the
strip over a finished recording.

# Custom encoder settings unlock when you choose Custom {stepper}
Under Settings › Advanced, picking Custom wrote the setting and left the two
numbers greyed out until you left the page and came back. They become editable
as you choose it.

# The background helper is reported for what it is {gear}
The helper is installed with the first meeting you arm and taken out again
with the last, so a Mac with nothing scheduled and no helper is a Mac in
order — it now says "Not needed, nothing is scheduled" in grey instead of
warning about it in amber, and Automation health reads Ready. A helper that is
plainly running is no longer reported as missing: RecordLah reads the mark the
helper itself writes every minute rather than only asking launchd whether the
job is registered. And the advice that came with the warning no longer tells
you to turn on a setting that is already on.

highlights.text: Under Settings › Advanced, picking Custom wrote the setting and left the two numbers greyed out until you left the page and came back. They become editable as you choose it.

highlights.title: The background helper is reported for what it is
highlights.text: The helper is installed with the first meeting you arm and taken out again with the last, so a Mac with nothing scheduled and no helper is a Mac in order — it now says "Not needed, nothing is scheduled" in grey instead of warning about it in amber, and Automation health reads Ready. A helper that is plainly running is no longer reported as missing: RecordLah reads the mark the helper itself writes every minute rather than only asking launchd whether the job is registered. And the advice that came with the warning no longer tells you to turn on a setting that is already on.
